newsitem.title: NORWAY: Scientists stumped in McDonald's Norway mystery.
newsitem.headline: Scientists stumped in McDonald's Norway mystery.

text.p: Norwegian scientists were mystified Friday by an apparent food poisoning outbreak that hospitalized four people and forced U.S. fast-food giant McDonald's Corp. to withdraw its McLaks salmon burgers in Norway.
John Kristian Taerud, head of the Municipal Food Control Authority in Stroemmen, near Oslo, said analysis of several samples of McLaks had failed to uncover the source of the poisoning.
He said his team would confer with the national Norwegian Food Control Authority and researchers at the University of Oslo next week.

"We will discuss what steps we should take next. We know from blood controls that these people were sick from a form of poisoning, but we have not been able to discover what it was," Taerud said in an interview.

McDonald's withdrew salmon burgers from all 36 branches in Norway after two customers and two employees apparently became ill Sunday after eating McLaks meals at a restaurant in Loerenskog outside Oslo.
The four were taken to hospital complaining of paralysis in the mouth, burning sensations, trembling, itching and rashes. All four have since been released.
Taerud said tests to date had concentrated on detecting biological chemicals which are produced when bacteria absorb a natural substance found in most fish.
At certain levels in the body, the chemicals, known as amines, cause symptoms similar to those described by the four patients, he said.

McDonald's spokeswoman in Norway, Agnete Samdahl, said the company had withdrawn the product as a precaution until the situation had been clarified, but it continued to have confidence in Norwegian salmon.
"We really believe in this product and we have great faith in Norwegian salmon," Samdahl said.
